claims.text: THE SIZES HAVE DRIFTED, AND THE DRIFT RUNS ONE WAY, across three opened documents. The 1990 interview notes give 'The small one was like 20 ft, the next 60 ft. diameter and the next one,...maybe 120 ft. diam. Just a guess; don't hold me to that.' The April 2001 Briefing Document gives the smallest as 'about 24 feet in diameter at its widest part, right at the base', the next as '60 feet in diameter at the base', and 'the largest of these vehicles was about 120 to 130 feet in diameter'. The arvp.co.uk FLUX 1988 page, read 18 September 2026, gives 'one with a 130-foot diameter, another with a 60-foot diameter, and a smaller one measuring 24 feet in diameter', with no disclaimer. Each retelling is more precise than the last about a figure the witness explicitly refused to stand behind.

Unfortunately, now that Mark has passed on it's impossible to get hold of. I imagine that Steven Greer may have it or at least a copy.'

claims.text: The site names no owner, author or organisation anywhere on the pages opened. Its footer gives only 'Email: Flux_liners@icloud.com', a 'Privacy Policy' link and 'Site by Blueqube' pointing at https://blueqube.org.uk . It carries no copyright notice and no licence statement of any kind on the FLUX 1988, TECH or SHOP pages.

claims.text: The 3D reconstruction is the site operator's own work, built from secondary material and not from the original drawing. The page states: 'This is my 3D recreation of the craft they described. I rebuilt it from the ground up, using measurements from the original sketches and information provided by Mark in his talks and videos', and, for a second version, 'using measurements from the original sketches and information provided by Mark from online live streams and podcast apperences.'
